title: Khwarezmid Dynasty
capsule: The Khwarezmid (Anushteginid) dynasty was a Turkic dynasty that began as governors of Khwarezm under Seljuq suzerainty, appointed by Anushtegin Gharchai around 1077, before Tekish (r. 1172–1200) transformed the line into independent sovereigns by defeating the last Seljuq sultan Toghrul III in 1194. Under Ala ad-Din Muhammad II (r. 1200–1220) the Khwarezmian Empire rapidly expanded to encompass Transoxiana, Khorasan, Afghanistan, and Persia, briefly making it the largest state in the Islamic world. The empire disintegrated with catastrophic speed after Genghis Khan launched his western campaign in 1219 following a diplomatic incident; Muhammad II died a fugitive in 1220, and Khwarezmian resistance collapsed by 1221, with the last sultan Jalal ad-Din Mingburnu fighting rearguard actions until his death in 1231.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The Khwarezmian Empire's core provinces are documented in Islamic geographical and administrative sources (Yaqut, Juzjani); the maximum territorial extent c. 1215–1219 is reconstructed from conquest narratives and is broadly reliable, though outer tributary borders are approximate.
